title: Matched ozone reproduction dose signs differed in two US papers, but joint mean intervals permitted either sign
abstract: We tested high-minus-low ozone concentration slopes in matched reproduction records from a 2024 public data release. Strict shared-control matching kept three series from two US papers published in 1999 and 2001. Equal-measure paper log slopes were -0.0921 and +0.6743 per 10 ppb. Their opposite point signs persisted under independent changes below 13.73% to each endpoint mean. However, joint t intervals for six endpoint means permitted either sign for every series. No eligible series came from Europe or the later publication period. These records did not establish a common reproduction dose slope or its transfer across regions and time. The sensitivity result concerns fixed means; the uncertainty result depends on source sample sizes and standard deviations. Selected pest outcomes, small samples, mixed reproductive measures and missing exposure duration limit inference. No climate interaction is tested. The package contains original code, new aggregate contrasts, source provenance, a figure and independent numeric checks. Raw source records remain external.

display.caption: Matched endpoint dose slopes and exact relative-mean changes that permit a zero paper mean. All joint sampling slope intervals span the full real line under the stated t assumptions.
